title: Shim noul answer shape cannot satisfy both DeskMind/JevBench and Typed Decisions
detail: Spec says 'map noul to a 2-option choice' but the three scorers read noul differently. DeskMind to_answer and JevBench typesafe read only the scalar answer['noul'] (=P(true)); the official Typed Decisions scorer ignores 'noul' and reads answer['probabilities'] (yes/no or true/false keys). A shim that copies DeskMind's shape scores every Typed Decisions noul as uniform -> argmax index 0 = 'false': 600/2000 decisions (30%) become base-rate guesses with max-entropy KL. Also 200/600 Typed Decisions noul questions send criteria=null, which a strict schema copied from DeskMind types may reject. JevBench validate_probs demands exact key-set equality, so extra keys inside choice/score 'probabilities' fail strict validity.
evidence: deskmind-ai/brain types.py:114-118 returns {'type':'noul','noul':dist['true']}; jevbench adapters/typesafe.py:86-91 p=float(ans['noul']) -> {'yes':p,'no':1-p}; typed-decisions bench/score_with_jobs.py:29-37 maps yes/no->true/false then p=[pred['probabilities'].get(o,0.0)...], s==0 -> uniform, am_p=p.index(max(p)); test.parquet: noul criteria types {dict:400, None:200}, gold keys ('false','true') x600; jevbench scoring.py:36-37 set(labels)==set(probs).
fix: noul answer = {'type':'noul','noul':p_true,'probabilities':{'false':1-p_true,'true':p_true},'confidence':...}; schema: noul criteria optional/nullable; choice/score 'probabilities' keys exactly = request option keys in request order (no extras); add a test that pipes each saved example's answer through the three upstream scorer functions (vendored) and asserts non-uniform parse.

title: DeskMind payloads exceed 58-option one-token alphabet; no overflow strategy specified
detail: generic_decide must reuse AlphaChoiceRenderer (spec), whose id alphabet is <=58 one-token ids (AGENTS.md). DeskMind protocol allows up to 255 options and its real replay fixture has 30% of choice questions above 58 options (max 240, e.g. element-target heads). Without a defined strategy the shim will either crash, 400, or silently truncate options -> the correct target is unrepresentable and DeskMind replay/bench accuracy is wrong while looking valid.
evidence: deskmind-ai/brain types.py:18 MAX_CHOICE_OPTIONS = 255, :51-52; fixtures/replay/v1/large.jsonl.gz: 30 records, 200 choice questions, 60 with >58 options, max 240, up to 7 questions/request (computed locally); decision.py:153 IDS = A-Z+0-9+a-z filtered to one-token, :164 requires >=40.
fix: In generic_decide: if n_opts > len(ids), run a tournament: chunk options into groups of len(ids)-1 in request order, score each chunk (one forward pass each, shared state snapshot), keep top chunk winners, final round; renormalise P(option)=P(chunk winner path) and record 'overflow_rounds' in the answer/trace. Never truncate; add a test with a 240-option fixture asserting all keys present and sum==1.

title: Per-question Decider + options-in-system re-prefills large state per question
detail: Spec backend is decide(state, question) one question at a time, rendered like DecisionEngine.route, which puts the options in the SYSTEM message and the request/state after them. For benchmark payloads the options differ per question and the state is the large part (DeskMind page+elements, Typed Decisions traces), so nothing useful is cacheable: each of the 5 Typed Decisions questions (up to 7 DeskMind heads) re-prefills the full state. That violates AGENTS.md ('each question is prefilled on a snapshot of the cached state, so extra questions cost only their own tokens') and multiplies the latency we report against DeskMind/typed-decisions by ~#questions.
evidence: builder_bench.md:21 'def decide(self, state: str, question: dict)'; decision.py:171 'the SYSTEM message (static prefix), request in the USER message', :186 ROUTE_SYSTEM.format(choices=...); typed-decisions test: 2000 decisions/400 cases = 5 q/request; DeskMind large fixture up to 7 q/request. Calculation: 1500-token state x5 questions = 7500 prefill tokens vs ~1500+5x~150 with state-first snapshotting.
fix: Decider.decide_all(state, questions) -> {qid: dist}; render [system: generic instructions] [user: state] then snapshot KV once, and per question append a suffix containing instructions+criteria+'choice#' prefill on a deepcopy of the snapshot. Keep decide() as a thin wrapper.

title: DeskMind comparison not pinned to suite, locale, or regradable run format
detail: DeskMind's published numbers come from diag-v25 (hands 3d54492), zh-Hans locale, Peekaboo 4.3.0, tasks written in Chinese, regraded from on-disk runs via 'deskmind-bench score'. The spec only says run 'their own published commands' and Muselet with its own loop; it does not pin suite version/locale, require --repeats 3 for all configs, or require Muselet runs to be written in the Hands run format that 'deskmind-bench score' regrades (strict pass, false DONE, DONE timing). Mixing suite versions/locales or grading Muselet with a different scorer makes the headline 'beats DeskMind' claim non-comparable.
evidence: deskmind-ai/bench README.md:65 'deskmind-bench score path/to/runs/ --suite-version diag-v25'; :126 'diag-v25 | 3d54492 | current'; :137-138 'Apple M4 Pro, macOS 27, zh-Hans locale, Peekaboo 4.3.0. The tasks are written in Chinese'; builder_bench.md lines 1-12 contain no suite/locale/repeat pin.
fix: bench/deskmind/README.md: pin --suite-version diag-v25 and hands commit; run DeskMind and Muselet in the same locale on the same Mac (state which), 3 repeats each, all runs kept; Muselet adapter writes run.json/trace in the Hands record layout and is graded only by 'deskmind-bench score' (same scorer for both); report the suite hash in the results table.

title: Latency compared across incompatible definitions (model-only vs end-to-end)
detail: DeskMind aggregate.latency_s is planner time per decision; HobbyLM's headline latency is model time per decision (live total elapsed reported separately); Typed Decisions latency is HTTP request time; Muselet replay records utterance->first action and ->verified completion. Putting these in one table either understates competitors (their model-only vs our end-to-end) or overstates us. The fairness rule 'latency measured end to end the same way for everyone' is not implementable from the spec as written.
evidence: deskmind-ai/bench docs/scoring.md:24 '`aggregate.latency_s` | p50 / p95 of the planner's time per decision'; hobbymac_score.py reports model latency and total elapsed separately; builder_bench.md:46-47 Muselet: 'time from utterance to first action and to verified completion'.
fix: Every runner records, for every system on the same Mac: (a) per-decision model time, (b) per-task wall time from request submission to verified final state (harness-measured, same clock). Results tables label columns (a)/(b); never compare against published numbers from other hardware.

title: HobbyLM replay graders must reuse HobbyLM per-kind criteria, pre-registered
detail: HobbyLM's 90/125 uses per-kind rules: calc = said DONE AND display correct AND every typed chunk ends with '='; none (16 tasks) = FIRST action UNKNOWN (no state check); device = direction + DONE; event = calendar read-back. Spec says grade 'by final Mac state', which is undefined for 'none' requests (Muselet will ANSWER/REFUSE/web-search) and stricter/looser than HobbyLM for calc/device. If the mapping (e.g. Muselet REFUSE/ANSWER == UNKNOWN pass) is chosen after seeing results, it is cherry-picking; if HobbyLM is graded by its scorer and Muselet by ours, the comparison is unfair.
evidence: hobbylm hobbymac_run.py:278-297: completed = said_done and correct; clean requires typed endswith('='); none: correct = steps[0]['parsed'].get('kind') == 'UNKNOWN'; r4 set kinds: calc 30, event 30, none 16, device 15, app 10, timer 8, dark 6, folder 6, screenshot 4.
fix: bench/hobbylm/graders.py: one grader per kind applied identically to HobbyLM and Muselet runs (final-state check + DONE claim), with a committed, pre-registered mapping table for 'none' (Muselet ASK/REFUSE/ANSWER-without-OS-action = pass; any OS action = fail) and device direction tasks; report both HobbyLM-scorer and strict-state numbers.

title: HobbyLM event replay can send real calendar invites from lead's account
detail: 30/125 r4 tasks are EVENT, many with invitee emails (example.com in published sets). HobbyLM documents that confirming such an event sends a real invitation from the chosen calendar. An unattended replay that auto-answers Muselet's CONFIRM (or HobbyLM's y/n) on the lead's Mac will send invitations from the lead's iCloud/Google calendar and leave events behind, also contaminating later tasks (setup/teardown not isolated).
evidence: hobbylm README.md:288 'Real invites. If the event has an email address, confirming it sends a real invitation from the calendar you chose.'; :215 'emails replaced by example.com'; spec builder_bench.md:44-47 has no calendar isolation or confirm policy.
fix: replay.py: create a local 'On My Mac' calendar 'muselet-bench' in setup, force create_event/HobbyLM to target it, strip/rewrite attendee addresses to a non-delivering form for execution while grading the parsed invitee, delete the calendar in teardown; refuse to run event tasks unless that calendar is the target (assert before confirm).

title: Latency compared across incompatible definitions (model-only vs end-to-end)
evidence: Replay implements different clocks per system. Muselet: utterance_latency_s = monotonic time until the poll loop exits (:286), which includes waiting for the trace line plus 0.2 s sleeps. completion_latency_s comes from a poll that runs helper.snapshot() (osascript to System Events, Calculator and Finder) during Muselet's run (:240-247), adding load and AX contention that the HobbyLM path never has. HobbyLM: utterance_latency_s = its own seconds_total and completion_latency_s = seconds_total if correct (:436-438).
fix: Use one external clock for both systems: start = subprocess spawn, end = first poll where final state is correct, polled the same way (lightweight, e.g. 0.25 s, same probes) for both. Or report only each system's internal timestamps and label them.

title: Muselet event grade never checks the created event's date/time/invitee
detail: For Muselet event tasks, replay checks that some event with the title returned by create_event exists in 'Hobby Test', then calls helper.event_matches(record['text'], expected). That compares the REQUEST text to the expected answer, which is constant per task and independent of what Muselet did. A Muselet event on the wrong day, time or timezone, or with the wrong invitee, passes. That is up to 30/125 r4 tasks graded on title only, a wrong result presented as correct in the head-to-head. Upstream event_matches(got, exp) compares the model's EVENT output against expected.

The first argument is supposed to be the system's output.

title: Chunked combine can contradict stage-two winner and miscalibrate
detail: combine_chunked sets P(label) = P(label | chunk) * P_stage2(chunk winner). The combined argmax can then pick a different option than the stage-two head-to-head picked, and the probability mass of chunks with flat conditionals is underweighted. That affects accuracy and calibration (Brier/ECE) on exactly the >58-option DeskMind questions, 60/200 in the large fixture.
evidence: Calculation: chunk1 conditional {a:.34,b:.33,c:.33}, chunk2 {d:.9,e:.1}; stage two {a:.6, d:.4}. Combined a=.204, d=.36, so the answer is d even though stage two preferred a by 0.6 vs 0.4.
fix: Use the stage-two pick as the answer: answer = argmax stage2. For probabilities, give the stage-two winner its stage-two mass and spread the rest proportionally, e.g. P(x in chunk k) = P2(w_k) * p_k(x)/p_k(w_k) renormalized. Or, more simply, return the stage-two distribution over winners and zero elsewhere.

title: Runtime zoom re-crops the 1 MP shot; bench zoom gain won't transfer
detail: Grounder defaults to zoom=True and locate() crops stage 2 out of the same image file it was given. At runtime that file is the HandsKit screenshot already capped at ~1 MP (AGENTS.md screenshot max_pixels:1000000), so the zoom crop holds no pixels stage 1 did not already see at the same resolution: about 2x latency for no extra detail. The harness, though, feeds native ScreenSpot-Pro images (mostly 4K) and crops from the full-resolution source, so the crop carries about 2.3x more pixels than stage 1 saw. Any 'with zoom' SSPro number will overstate what the runtime gets. zoom_region() (fresh high-res `screenshot {region}`) exists but nothing calls it except a unit test.
evidence: grounder.py:431 `zoom: bool = True`; :479-483 `zb = self.zoom_box(first.point, image.size)` -> `self.ground(image, ...)` on the same PIL image; :507-511 locate() opens image_path once. `grep -rn zoom_region ml/src bench` -> only the def (:141) and ml/tests/test_grounder.py:99-104. Calculation, SSPro 3840x2160: stage 1 smart_resize to <=1 MP (~0.12x pixels); zoom 0.4 crop = 1536x864 = 1.33 MP -> ~1 MP, i.e. ~8x stage-1 pixel density. Runtime 1 MP shot: crop 0.4 -> ~0.16-0.24 MP at the same density as stage 1, so stage 2 gains 0x.
fix: Make locate() zoom only when the source has more pixels than max_pixels, else default zoom off. Add a two-shot runtime path: brain calls screenshot{region: zoom_region(pt, shot)} and grounds that crop, mapping back via its own origin/scale. In run_screenspot.py add `--source-max-pixels 1000000`: downscale the SSPro image before both stages, so 'zoom' results mirror the runtime unless the two-shot path is used.

So overlapping screenshots or instructions would pass unchecked. Today this is P1 because no grounding data is built yet. It becomes P0 the moment a Phase-4 grounding set is generated without an image or instruction filter.

Extend decontam to drop grounding training rows whose instruction n-gram matches, or whose screenshot phash is within Hamming <=6 of any eval image. Fail closed if the export is missing.

title: --limit takes first N sorted rows: single-app, unrepresentative subsets
detail: select() truncates after loading annotation files in sorted filename order. So `--limit 100` on ScreenSpot-Pro evaluates only the alphabetically first application(s). The README's quick runs (used to pick a model under time pressure) would then compare candidates on one app/group rather than the 1,581-sample mix. Per-group accuracy varies widely across SSPro groups, so model ranking can flip.
evidence: run_screenspot.py:146-148 `for f in sorted((root/'annotations').glob('*.json')): rows.extend(...)`; :138 `return out[:limit] if limit else out`. With 1,581 samples over 26 apps (~60/app), --limit 50 is one app.
fix: Use a stratified sample when --limit is set, e.g. round-robin by (group, ui_type) with a fixed seed, and record the seed and sample ids in the run summary.

title: Latency clocks still differ between Muselet and HobbyLM
detail: The shared harness migration gives Muselet completion = first poll where the checks pass (verified_latency_s). title: Teacher demo runner does not exclude planner v2 holdout states

title: Planner v2 gold rewards field-replacing type as an append
detail: 8 v2 scenarios (5 in v2-holdout: v2-notes-text-missing, v2-doc-sysprompt, v2-pages-append, v2-note-checklist-item, v2-pages-type-save; 3 in v2-tune) use gold replies and accept_first patterns that 'append' with `type #ref "\n..."`. So these cases score a reply that erases the user's existing note/document text as a pass, and a planner that obeys rule 17 (types existing value + new text) may fail accept_first patterns anchored on the clobbering form. This inflates/deflates v2-holdout in the wrong direction on exactly the destructive-edit behaviour the safety rules forbid, and tuning on v2-tune would reward it. planner-demos' keep.py protects the demo data with a clobber filter, but the benchmark itself is unchanged.

fix: Rewrite gold/accept for the 8 cases to the non-destructive form the prompt requires (existing value + new text, or a skill that inserts at the cursor), add the clobber check from keep.py to planner_offline.grade as a reject rule, and re-run any v2 numbers. Don't quote v2-holdout until fixed.

title: EventKit date parse probably still fails: inputs carry a UTC offset and microseconds, and neither parser in 55e38f9 accepts both (unverified, needs Mac)
detail: _calendar_window builds start/end with datetime.now(ZoneInfo(helper.LOCAL_TZ)) (LOCAL_TZ='Asia/Kolkata' upstream), so isoformat() gives an offset-aware string with microseconds, e.g. '2026-10-23T19:32:06.268213+05:30'. They aren't naive, as the commit says. The Swift parseDate tries (1) ISO8601DateFormatter with default options, which has no .withFractionalSeconds; (2) a DateFormatter 'yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSSSS' with no zone field; (3) the same without fraction. My reading is that none of these accepts fraction+offset, which would mean exit(3), so every event/none-kind task gets an 'EventKit calendar snapshot failed' precondition error and is skipped for Muselet only. That would compound bench-16 (asymmetric denominators). Also, parseDate permanently mutates local.dateFormat after its first miss. The upstream helper has no calendar_events(), so this Swift fallback is the live path.
evidence: python3: datetime.now(ZoneInfo(...)).isoformat() -> '2026-10-23T19:32:06.268213-07:00'. git grep 'def calendar_events' bench/hobbylm/upstream -> none, so _calendar_events falls back to _read_calendar_events. Swift parsing behaviour not run (Linux).
fix: Pass start.isoformat(timespec='seconds') (offset kept) and set parser.formatOptions = [.withInternetDateTime] (or add .withFractionalSeconds). Add a Mac smoke test that the snapshot returns exit 0 for an aware datetime, and count event-kind skips per system in the report.
